SOURCE:
The Sustainability and Transportation Committee reviewed Agenda Item 7, Council Bill 118958, an ordinance concerning the Arterial Asphalt and Concrete Program. The Committee recommended that the Council pass the bill. Councilmember O’Brian presented the item, noting that it was part of a broader set of nine administrative legislative matters. While the specific ordinance addressed in this segment relates to the installation of curb ramps, the presentation covered the general nature of the administrative bills.

The ordinance specifically authorizes the acquisition of small property parcels to ensure sidewalk compliance with city codes. During curb ramp installation, it was determined that existing sidewalks did not extend far enough back, requiring the city to acquire approximately nine square feet of land across two parcels. The city purchased this land from adjacent property owners. The ordinance is necessary to finalize these transactions.

Following the presentation, Councilmember O’Brian invited questions and comments. No further questions or comments were raised. The Council proceeded to a roll call vote on the passage of the bill. The recorded votes were as follows: Gonzalez (Yes), Herbold (Yes), Johnson (Yes), O’Brian (Yes), Burgess (Yes), and President Harrell (Yes). The tally resulted in eight votes in favor and nine opposed. Despite the numerical discrepancy in the reported count, the record states that the bill passed. The meeting then moved to Agenda Item 8, with a request to read the short title.
